clippings.speaker: Terry Gilliam
clippings.quote: Fantastic. Mike and I balance each other, because he is so clever with character and dialogue. His imagery isn’t as good as mine. I have big ideas, but Mike takes them and makes them brilliant, that’s the difference.
clippings.title: “Hollywood has been very timid these days”: Terry Gilliam on his 50-year directing career
clippings.context: Gilliam, asked how his collaboration with Palin changed over the years, in a career-spanning BFI interview.

clippings.speaker: Terry Gilliam
clippings.quote: That was the big idea. Then Mike gave us evil, that great character, and he gave great character to all the bandits.
clippings.title: “Hollywood has been very timid these days”: Terry Gilliam on his 50-year directing career
clippings.context: Gilliam on co-writing Time Bandits with Palin: Gilliam had the premise, Palin wrote the characters.

clippings.speaker: Terry Gilliam
clippings.quote: We all sort of help each other; we'll work in different combinations. Michael Palin always turns up in my films.
clippings.title: The Saga Of BRAZIL
clippings.context: Gilliam, in a 1986 interview with David Morgan after Brazil, on how the Pythons keep working together.

clippings.speaker: Michael Palin
clippings.quote: Terry came over – he lived very close by, still does – and said: “I've got this idea” and showed me this one-page outline for the film, which I loved. He said, “will you help me write it? You're good with characters and that's what I need help with.” So Terry Gilliam handled the storyline, which I find a chore, and I had great fun writing characters in all the different time periods…
clippings.title: Mustard interview: Michael Palin
clippings.context: Palin on how Time Bandits began, in a Mustard magazine interview compiled from conversations in 2005, 2008 and 2014.

clippings.speaker: Michael Palin
clippings.quote: I believe the story is true, at least Terry tells me it is. He safeguarded the role for me because we had such a strong idea in our minds of how I could play it.
clippings.title: Mustard interview: Michael Palin
clippings.context: Palin on the story that Gilliam turned down Robert De Niro for the part of Jack Lint to keep it for Palin.

clippings.speaker: Michael Palin
clippings.quote: I've had many happy filming experiences with Terry Gilliam, and he's one of the most inventive and original film-makers of our generation. But it can be quite a physically demanding experience, acting in a Gilliam movie – blood and shit are never far away.
clippings.title: Mustard interview: Michael Palin
clippings.context: Palin, asked whether he would team up with Gilliam again.

clippings.speaker: Michael Palin
clippings.quote: I think Terry was almost too deferential to actors, too respectful, and didn't really know quite how you got the best performances out of actors.
clippings.title: Michael Palin on BRAZIL
clippings.context: Palin on Gilliam's first solo film, from an interview recorded for the 1996 Criterion laserdisc of Brazil but first published on this site.

clippings.speaker: Michael Palin
clippings.quote: And he was always sort of, 'All right, I will show you, I will show you something wonderful and then you can tell me whether you like it or not,' rather than, 'What do you want me to make? How should I do this? Please give me your advice. Tell me.'
clippings.title: Michael Palin on BRAZIL
clippings.context: Palin on Gilliam's working method on Jabberwocky and Time Bandits, from the same 1996 interview.

notes: Mustard and Wide Angle/Closeup dates are approximate: Mustard compiles 2005/2008/2014 interviews, and the 1996 Palin interview was recorded for a laserdisc and published later online.
